tagline: Architecture-aware Specs, explicit Agent grants and independently checked results.
title: Concorde Framework

homepage.title: Specify the architecture. Guide your agents.
homepage.description: Concorde keeps your project's Specs at the center of AI-assisted development. Your Pi session reads Specs, answers questions and edits them with you, then calls Concorde's Operations one explicit step at a time. Model steps run as native Pi Agent calls or pi workflows and count only after the Host accepts their proposals; richer flows may be LangGraph Graphs. Evidence binds to current inputs; direct edits never supply successful review or completion.

features.title: Context and permission, managed around the Spec.

items.title: Read complete Module specifications.
items.description: Module documents explain purpose, terminology, correct use, design and relationships for a reader who does not know the code. Implementation documents hold the precise requirements, scenarios and contracts. Paired metadata binds entities to the files that realize them, and tests declare the scenarios they verify.

items.title: Give each Agent call exactly its context.
items.description: An Agent call receives four kinds of context: the Spec context its Module's declarations select, the names (and, for code phases, the contents) of its Module's files, the contracts of the tools it may use, and its task. A missing promise becomes a reported Spec gap, never a guess from code.

items.title: Distinguish grants from enforced isolation.
items.description: Domain Agents have fresh context and terminal tool ceilings. Native file, network and credential restrictions are prompt policy, not OS confinement. Only programmer receives a code-write grant. Configured checks and tester commands separately enforce read-only governing files with writable external scratch; unavailable isolation refuses execution.

items.title: Operations, Agents and two kinds of control flow.
items.description: An Operation is one cataloged entry: a Host service, a single Agent call, a pi workflow run by pi-subagents, or a LangGraph Graph built with the Graph API. Agents defines the seven domain Agents; the Pi session owns the two Task subagents. Every flow is explained in its owner's Spec by a step table or a Graph Spec.

items.title: Develop in candidate worktrees.
items.description: In consumer projects, a mutating capability requested from primary normally runs in a host-created candidate from the committed base; your session stays in place. Source maintenance uses a fresh catalog-free writer, then the user session selects independent testing and, when selected, a fresh sibling tester with exact candidate Pi entry, embedded catalog and runtime provenance. Evidence binds current inputs; delivery and primary merging remain separate requests.

items.title: Track problems as Issues.
items.description: Agents record attributed bugs, contract gaps and limitations as Git-versioned Issues. concorde-issues lists, shows, reports, reopens or solves one selected Issue; solving runs in a candidate, returns Spec repairs to the developer and closes an Issue only after checks.

workflow.title: Choose the result you need.
workflow.description: The calling agent chooses the target and order: read and edit the contract directly, then explicitly select context-solve, plan, tasks, implement, independent reviews and validation as needed. There is no automatic authoring, routing or development workflow.

steps.title: Read & select
steps.description: Read complete Module Specs, choose an explicit target, and reconcile authorized Spec, metadata and registry edits directly. Select independent Spec review separately.

steps.title: Plan & implement
steps.description: Confirm the contract suffices, plan and derive tasks from the Spec alone, then write only the Module's listed files.

steps.title: Validate & review
steps.description: Run configured checks and select independent code review. Blocking findings return to the caller, who chooses repair tasks or a stop.

steps.title: Ready, not merged
steps.description: Inspect the candidate. Delivery publishes its branch on request; merging primary needs a separate authorization.

quickstart.title: Start with an explicit project contract.
quickstart.description: Clone and build Concorde, then preview the installation into your Git project. Use Python 3.11+, Node.js 22.6+ with npm and the Pi coding agent with the supported native pi-subagents producer. Linux with bubblewrap is required for enforced check/tester execution, not a claim of native Agent confinement. Pi is the only supported client. Its concorde tool describes and prepares native capabilities or runs finite Host services; initialize the project with concorde-init after installation.
quickstart.code:
git clone https://github.com/FTOD/concorde.git
cd concorde
python3 scripts/concorde.py build

# Replace the path with your Git project.
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py \
  --target /absolute/path/to/project --preview

# Review the preview, then rerun with --apply.

reference.title: Agents and public capabilities
reference.description: Eleven Operations, all public, keep their concorde-* names. Agents defines seven domain Agents; the Pi session owns two Task subagents, of which consumer packages carry only the tester. Init, configure, validate and deliver make no model calls.

tables.title: Public capabilities
tables.description: Public entries pass common admission. Targeted entries require an explicit Module target. describe-policy previews applicable worker grants without execution; initialization instead uses its deterministic proposal preview.
rows: concorde-context-solve
Assess whether the explicitly selected contract supports the task without editing it.
concorde-plan
Assess current context and produce a revision-bound plan from Specs, not implementation contents.
concorde-tasks
Author acceptance tasks from a current plan; explicitly selected repair feedback must be current.
concorde-implement
Complete admitted local tasks within the listed code grant; return separately selected component work to the caller.
concorde-spec-review
Review the complete Spec and terminology semantic consistency without starting a development change.
concorde-code-review
Review or diagnose the granted implementation against its Spec without starting a development change.
concorde-issues
Inspect or assess an explicit Issue; return repairs to the caller and verify actual current evidence separately.
concorde-init
Propose and apply initialization with a pinned Protocol, the worker model and an honest Module stub.
concorde-configure
Apply explicit Pi worker model, thinking and timeout settings; accept an installed Protocol only when requested.
concorde-validate
Record current deterministic validation evidence for a candidate.
concorde-deliver
Publish a verified delivery branch and normally remove its source worktree; merge primary only on a separate request.

tables.title: Agents and Task subagents
tables.description: Agents defines each domain Agent once: tools, effects, instructions and output contract. Task subagents belong to the Pi session and receive explicit task and worktree grants. No Agent or Task subagent delegates.
rows: spec-reviewer, context-assessor
Review a Spec independently or assess whether its context suffices; read-only.
planner, task-author
Produce plans and acceptance tasks from the Spec, declared references and file names, without source contents.
programmer, code-reviewer
Write only the selected Module's listed files, or review the authorized code read-only in a fresh conversation.
issue-solver
Choose bounded work or an evidence-grounded disposition for one explicitly selected Issue.
maintenance-worker
Source-only author of verified candidate work under the user session's frozen grant; self-checks are not independent acceptance.
tester
Fresh source/consumer independent tester with read-only governing artifacts, enforced commands and retained evidence; never repairs or delegates.

tables.title: Modules
tables.description: Dependencies point inward: Spec tooling and Observation use nothing, the Harness never uses Operations or its providers, and outer Modules use what they need.
rows: Spec tooling
Load and check Specs, compute context and boundary sets, register typed values and propose the first Spec.
Harness
Admit requests, compose context, run Agent calls and workflows, run checks in the read-only boundary, manage candidate worktrees and observe timing. Native file policy is not a sandbox.
Agents
Define the seven domain Agents; the tools preflight allows come from these definitions.
Operations
Hold the Operation catalog and dispatch; its providers are Planning, Implementation, Review, Validation, Delivery and Issue solving.
Issues
Keep Issue records and the report service Agents use.
Pi session
Configure the developer's Pi session: the concorde tool, session selection, Task subagents and coordinator instructions.
Distribution
Build, check and install the package, provision the managed runtime and launch requests.
Views
Publish Module documents and Implementation documents as a navigable documentation site.

tables.title: Launchers and supporting tools
tables.description: Source-checkout commands are shown below. Installed projects use the corresponding scripts under .concorde/framework/. Direct CLI validation is distinct from lifecycle readiness evidence.
rows: python3 scripts/run-operation.py <operation> < invocation.json
Submit a typed request. Model-backed capabilities need the prepared native Pi transport; a bare CLI call refuses without it.
concorde tool in a Pi session
Describe the eleven public capabilities, prepare native Agent calls and workflows, or run Host services.
python3 scripts/concorde.py <command>

build, validate, check-package, select-session, protocol-manifest, registry, docsite and status: render assets, check the project and package, verify a private Pi selection, bind the Protocol, sync the registry, scaffold a docsite and coordinate change status.
python3 scripts/install-concorde.py
Preview or apply the Pi-only installation; files the installer owns are removed only when unchanged, and user content is preserved.
python3 scripts/issues.py
List, show or check Issues from the command line.
npm --prefix docsite run <script>
Start, build, validate, typecheck or test the documentation site.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest
Run deterministic Python tests in parallel without starting model-backed workers.
